target: cauline leaf (PO_0000013) absent. The basal rosette leaves (PO_0000014 rosette leaf) are present and rosulate.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent on the culm sheath, and trichome (PO_0000282, synonym seta) absent at the sheath apex (oral setae). The sheath bristles ('clavate-setose') belong to the leaf sheath (PO_0020104), not to a stipule.
fix: In Poaceae/bamboo descriptions 'auricles' are leaf sheath auricles (PO_0020106) and 'oral setae' (shoulder bristles) are trichomes at the sheath mouth. Neither is a stipule; grasses have no stipules. 'Sheath', 'culm sheath', 'auricle', 'oral setae' must never be grounded to PO_0020041.
reason: Grasses and bamboos have no stipules. Grounding auricles to stipule produces the absence, and the sheath's yellow setae, also put on 'stipule', produce the clash.

target: no annotation. 'Flowers not known' means the flowers are missing from the material, not absent from the plant. Cyme inflorescence present stays.
fix: '<part> not known / not seen / unknown / not observed / inconnu(e)s / non vu(e)s' means no data. Give no annotation, never '<part> absent'.
reason: The taxon was described from fruiting material. 1-fruited cymes show that flowers exist.

target: 'leafless' describes the flowering stem (scape). PO has no leafless-scape class, so give no annotation, or record it as the absence of cauline leaves (PO_0000013) on the flowering stem. 'persistent bases' is leaf base (PO_0020040) persistent, not the whole leaf.
fix: A bare 'leafless' or 'aphyllous' inside a stem, scape or peduncle clause negates leaves on that axis only. It is a taxon-level 'leaf absent' only when the plant description itself says the plant is leafless and no leaf characters follow.
reason: Iris curvifolia has basal leaves whose old bases persist as fibres. Only the flowering stem is leafless.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106) absent. 'sheath glabrous' belongs to leaf sheath (PO_0020104) glabrous (PATO_0000453), not to stipule.

target: lateral bracts on the fig receptacle wall absent. PO has no class for these, so give no annotation. The basal bracts at the receptacle base are present and parchment-like (bract PO_0009055 papyraceous).

target: the ray florets (neuter in Montanoa) have no style; the disc florets have a style. The context word is ray floret vs disc floret. Separately, 'non élargi à la base' (not widened at base) was wrongly annotated as style dilated; it should be negated or dropped.
fix: In Asteraceae, 'style absent' inside a ray floret clause ('fleurs ligulées / du rayon / neutres') is limited to those florets. Carry the floret context word and do not apply it to the taxon's style. Also, 'non <quality>' must never produce the positive quality.
reason: Montanoa has sterile ray florets without a style and fertile disc florets with a style that is bifid at the tip.

target: lateral bracts on the fig receptacle absent (no PO class, so give no annotation). The apical (ostiolar) bracts are present, incurved to erect.

target: no absence. 'almost leafless' says the (flowering) stems have few or reduced leaves. The basal leaves are dissected into 3-5 divisions.

target: palea reduced (small or vestigial), not absent. Also, 'without keels' was wrongly annotated as palea keel-shaped; it should be 'palea not keeled' or dropped.
